title: Soviet occupation of Ukraine
summary: The Soviet occupation of Ukraine encompasses various military actions and territorial changes involving Soviet forces from the early 20th century to the mid-20th century, significantly impacting the region's history and its relationship with the Soviet Union.

sections.heading: Ukrainian War of Independence (1917–1921)
paragraphs: The [[ukrainian-war-of-independence|Ukrainian War of Independence]] was a pivotal conflict occurring from 1917 to 1921, during which [[ukraine|Ukraine]] sought to establish itself as an independent nation amidst the chaos of World War I and the Russian Revolution.

sections.heading: Soviet Invasions of Ukraine (1918–1919)
paragraphs: The [[ukrainiansoviet-war|Soviet invasion of Ukraine]] in 1918 marked the beginning of direct military interventions by Soviet forces, followed by another invasion in 1919 that further entrenched Soviet influence in the region.
The [[kharkiv-oblast|Kharkiv]] Operation in December 1919 was a significant military engagement that aimed to consolidate Soviet control over Ukraine.

sections.heading: Annexations in the Late 1930s and 1940s
paragraphs: In 1939, [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]] annexed [[eastern-galicia|Eastern Galicia]] and [[volhynia|Volhynia]], expanding its territorial claims [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]].

The occupation of [[bessarabia|Bessarabia]] and Northern [[bukovina|Bukovina]] occurred in 1940, further illustrating the Soviet strategy of territorial expansion at the expense of [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] sovereignty.
The annexation of [[transcarpathia|Transcarpathia]] took place between 1944 and 1945, completing a series of territorial acquisitions by the Soviet regime in Ukraine.
